items.good: My brother is taller than my father.
items.ko: 내 남동생은 아버지보다 키가 커요.
bad: My brother is more tall than my father.
My brother is tallest than my father.
My brother is taller that my father.

cz.st: My brother is ___ than my father.

items.rule: 짧은 형용사의 비교급은 -er을 붙이고, 비교하는 대상 앞에는 than을 써요.

items.good: This is the longest bridge in our town.
items.ko: 이곳은 우리 마을에서 가장 긴 다리예요.
bad: This is the longer bridge in our town.
This is the most long bridge in our town.
This is longest bridge in our town.

cz.st: This is the ___ bridge in our town.

items.rule: 셋 이상 중 '가장 ~한'은 the + -est로 나타내요. 짧은 형용사에는 most를 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Today is hotter than yesterday.
items.ko: 오늘은 어제보다 더 더워요.
bad: Today is hoter than yesterday.
Today is more hot than yesterday.
Today is hottest than yesterday.

cz.st: Today is ___ than yesterday.

items.rule: '단모음 + 단자음'으로 끝나는 형용사는 마지막 자음을 한 번 더 쓰고 -er을 붙여요 (hot → hotter).

items.good: The red bag is bigger than the blue one.
items.ko: 빨간 가방이 파란 것보다 더 커요.
bad: The red bag is biger than the blue one.
The red bag is bigger as the blue one.
The red bag is bigest than the blue one.

cz.st: The red bag is ___ than the blue one.

items.rule: big처럼 '단모음 + 단자음'으로 끝나면 자음을 겹쳐 쓰고 -er을 붙여요. 비교할 때는 than을 써요.

items.good: I feel happier today than last week.
items.ko: 나는 지난주보다 오늘 더 행복해요.
bad: I feel happyer today than last week.
I feel happy today than last week.
I feel happiest today than last week.

cz.st: I feel ___ today than last week.

items.rule: '자음 + y'로 끝나는 형용사는 y를 i로 바꾸고 -er을 붙여요 (happy → happier).

items.good: This puzzle is easier than the last one.
items.ko: 이 퍼즐은 지난번 것보다 쉬워요.
bad: This puzzle is easyer than the last one.
This puzzle is easiest than the last one.
This puzzle is easy than the last one.

cz.st: This puzzle is ___ than the last one.

items.rule: y로 끝나는 형용사는 y를 i로 바꾸고 -er을 붙여요 (easy → easier). than이 있으면 비교급이에요.

items.good: Friday was the busiest day of my week.
items.ko: 금요일은 내 한 주에서 가장 바쁜 날이었어요.
bad: Friday was the busyest day of my week.
Friday was the busier day of my week.
Friday was busiest day of my week.

cz.st: Friday was the ___ day of my week.

items.rule: y를 i로 바꾸고 -est를 붙이며(busy → busiest), 최상급 앞에는 the를 써요.

items.good: Her new house is nicer than her old one.
items.ko: 그녀의 새 집은 예전 집보다 더 좋아요.
bad: Her new house is niceer than her old one.
Her new house is nice than her old one.
Her new house is nicest than her old one.

cz.st: Her new house is ___ than her old one.

items.rule: e로 끝나는 형용사는 -r만 붙여요 (nice → nicer, nicest).

items.good: That is the largest room in the museum.
items.ko: 저곳은 박물관에서 가장 큰 방이에요.
bad: That is the largeest room in the museum.
That is the larger room in the museum.
That is largest room in the museum.

cz.st: That is the ___ room in the museum.

items.rule: e로 끝나는 형용사는 -st만 붙이고(large → largest), 최상급 앞에는 the를 써요.

items.good: The new phone is more expensive than the old one.
items.ko: 새 휴대폰은 예전 것보다 더 비싸요.
bad: The new phone is expensiver than the old one.
The new phone is most expensive than the old one.
The new phone is more expensive then the old one.

cz.st: The new phone is ___ expensive than the old one.

items.rule: 길고 어려운 형용사는 -er 대신 more를 앞에 붙여 비교급을 만들어요. 최상급 most와 than은 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: This book is more interesting than that movie.
items.ko: 이 책은 저 영화보다 더 흥미로워요.
bad: This book is interestinger than that movie.
This book is most interesting than that movie.
This book is more interesting as that movie.

cz.st: This book is more ___ than that movie.

items.rule: 3음절 이상 형용사는 more + 원급으로 비교급을 만들어요. 사물이 흥미를 주면 interesting이에요.

items.good: Safety is the most important rule of all.
items.ko: 안전은 모든 규칙 중에서 가장 중요한 규칙이에요.
bad: Safety is the importantest rule of all.
Safety is the more important rule of all.
Safety is most important rule of all.

cz.st: Safety is the ___ important rule of all.

items.rule: 긴 형용사의 최상급은 the most + 원급이에요.

items.good: This is the most delicious soup I have ever had.
items.ko: 이것은 내가 먹어 본 수프 중 가장 맛있어요.
bad: This is the deliciousest soup I have ever had.
This is the more delicious soup I have ever had.
This is most delicious soup I have ever had.

cz.st: This is the most ___ soup I have ever had.

items.rule: delicious처럼 긴 형용사는 most를 붙여 최상급을 만들고, 앞에 the를 써요. 'I have ever had'는 경험 중 최고라는 뜻이에요.

items.good: Minji speaks English better than her brother.
items.ko: 민지는 오빠보다 영어를 더 잘해요.
bad: Minji speaks English gooder than her brother.
Minji speaks English more good than her brother.
Minji speaks English best than her brother.

cz.st: Minji speaks English ___ than her brother.

items.rule: good/well의 비교급은 불규칙 형태인 better예요 (good - better - best).

items.good: That was the worst storm of the year.
items.ko: 그것은 올해 최악의 폭풍이었어요.
bad: That was the baddest storm of the year.
That was the most bad storm of the year.
That was the worse storm of the year.

cz.st: That was the ___ storm of the year.

items.rule: bad의 최상급은 worst예요 (bad - worse - worst).

items.good: My cold is worse today than yesterday.
items.ko: 내 감기는 어제보다 오늘 더 심해요.
bad: My cold is badder today than yesterday.
My cold is more bad today than yesterday.
My cold is worst today than yesterday.

cz.st: My cold is ___ today than yesterday.

items.rule: bad의 비교급은 worse예요. than이 있으면 비교급을 써요.

items.good: I have more books than my cousin.
items.ko: 나는 사촌보다 책이 더 많아요.
bad: I have many books than my cousin.
I have most books than my cousin.
I have manier books than my cousin.

cz.st: I have ___ books than my cousin.

items.rule: many/much의 비교급은 more예요 (many - more - most).

items.good: She drinks less milk than her sister.
items.ko: 그녀는 언니보다 우유를 덜 마셔요.
bad: She drinks little milk than her sister.
She drinks lesser milk than her sister.
She drinks least milk than her sister.

cz.st: She drinks ___ milk than her sister.

items.rule: little의 비교급은 less예요. milk는 셀 수 없는 명사라 fewer는 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Jisu spent the least money on the trip.
items.ko: 지수는 여행에서 돈을 가장 적게 썼어요.
bad: Jisu spent the littlest money on the trip.
Jisu spent the less money on the trip.
Jisu spent the most little money on the trip.

cz.st: Jisu spent the ___ money on the trip.

items.rule: little의 최상급은 least예요 (little - less - least). money는 셀 수 없는 명사예요.

items.good: My bag is as heavy as yours.
items.ko: 내 가방은 네 것만큼 무거워요.
bad: My bag is as heavier as yours.
My bag is so heavy as yours.
My bag is as heavy than yours.

cz.st: My bag is as ___ as yours.

items.rule: 'as + 원급 + as'는 '~만큼 …한'이라는 뜻이고, 형용사는 원래 형태 그대로 써요.

items.good: This soup is not as hot as that one.
items.ko: 이 수프는 저것만큼 뜨겁지 않아요.
bad: This soup is not as hotter as that one.
This soup is not as hot than that one.
This soup is not as hot that one.

cz.st: This soup is not as hot ___ that one.

items.rule: 'not as + 원급 + as'는 '~만큼 …하지 않은'이에요. 뒤의 as를 than으로 바꾸지 않아요.

items.good: This train is twice as fast as that bus.
items.ko: 이 기차는 저 버스보다 두 배 빨라요.
bad: This train is twice as faster as that bus.
This train is twice faster as that bus.
This train is twice as fast than that bus.

cz.st: This train is twice as ___ as that bus.

items.rule: '배수 + as + 원급 + as'로 몇 배인지 나타내요. 가운데 형용사는 원급이에요.

items.good: A bike is much cheaper than a car.
items.ko: 자전거는 자동차보다 훨씬 더 싸요.
bad: A bike is very cheaper than a car.
A bike is more cheaper than a car.
A bike is much cheap than a car.

cz.st: A bike is ___ cheaper than a car.

items.rule: 비교급을 강조할 때는 much, a lot, far, even을 쓰고 very는 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: The test was even harder than I expected.
items.ko: 시험은 내가 예상한 것보다 훨씬 더 어려웠어요.
bad: The test was even hardest than I expected.
The test was even more harder than I expected.
The test was even hard than I expected.

cz.st: The test was even ___ than I expected.

items.rule: even은 비교급을 강조해요. harder에 more를 또 붙이는 이중 비교급은 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: The more you practice, the better you play.
items.ko: 연습을 많이 할수록 더 잘하게 돼요.
bad: The more you practice, better you play.
More you practice, the better you play.
The more you practice, the best you play.

cz.st: The more you practice, the ___ you play.

items.rule: 'the + 비교급 ~, the + 비교급 …'은 '~할수록 더 …하다'라는 뜻이에요. 앞뒤 모두 the를 써요.

items.good: The older we get, the wiser we become.
items.ko: 나이가 들수록 우리는 더 현명해져요.
bad: The older we get, wiser we become.
The oldest we get, the wisest we become.
Older we get, the wiser we become.

cz.st: The older we get, the ___ we become.

items.rule: 'the + 비교급 ~, the + 비교급 …' 구문에서 두 부분 모두 the + 비교급이에요.

items.good: It is getting darker and darker outside.
items.ko: 바깥이 점점 더 어두워지고 있어요.
bad: It is getting dark and dark outside.
It is getting darker or darker outside.
It is getting darkest and darkest outside.

cz.st: It is getting ___ and darker outside.

items.rule: '비교급 and 비교급'은 '점점 더 ~한'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.good: The movie became more and more exciting.
items.ko: 영화는 점점 더 흥미진진해졌어요.
bad: The movie became more exciting and exciting.
The movie became most and most exciting.
The movie became more and more excited.

cz.st: The movie became more and more ___.

items.rule: 긴 형용사는 'more and more + 원급'으로 '점점 더'를 나타내요. 영화가 흥미를 주므로 exciting이에요.

items.good: This is one of the biggest parks in our city.
items.ko: 이곳은 우리 도시에서 가장 큰 공원 중 하나예요.
bad: This is one of the biggest park in our city.
This is one of the most big parks in our city.
This is one of biggest parks in our city.

cz.st: This is one of the biggest ___ in our city.

items.rule: 'one of the + 최상급' 뒤에는 복수 명사가 와요.

items.good: Ms. Kim is one of the most popular teachers in our school.
items.ko: 김 선생님은 우리 학교에서 가장 인기 있는 선생님들 중 한 분이에요.
bad: Ms. Kim is one of the most popular teacher in our school.
Ms. Kim is one of most popular teachers in our school.
Ms. Kim is one of the popularest teachers in our school.

cz.st: Ms. Kim is one of the ___ popular teachers in our school.

items.rule: 'one of the most + 형용사 + 복수 명사'는 '가장 ~한 …들 중 하나'예요.

items.good: Minho is the tallest of the four players.
items.ko: 민호는 네 명의 선수 중 키가 가장 커요.
bad: Minho is the tallest in the four players.
Minho is the taller of the four players.
Minho is tallest of the four players.

cz.st: Minho is the tallest ___ the four players.

items.rule: 최상급 뒤에 복수 대상이 오면 of, 장소나 집단이 오면 in을 써요.

items.good: Jiho is the fastest runner in his class.
items.ko: 지호는 반에서 가장 빠른 달리기 선수예요.
bad: Jiho is the fastest runner than his class.
Jiho is the most fast runner in his class.
Jiho is the faster runner in his class.

cz.st: Jiho is the fastest runner ___ his class.

items.rule: 최상급 뒤에는 범위를 나타내는 in(집단·장소)을 쓰고, than은 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Please walk more carefully on the stairs.
items.ko: 계단에서는 더 조심해서 걸어 주세요.
bad: Please walk more careful on the stairs.
Please walk carefuller on the stairs.
Please walk most carefully on the stairs.

cz.st: Please walk more ___ on the stairs.

items.rule: -ly로 끝나는 부사는 more를 붙여 비교급을 만들어요 (carefully → more carefully).

items.good: Sora arrives earlier than her friends.
items.ko: 소라는 친구들보다 더 일찍 도착해요.
bad: Sora arrives more early than her friends.
Sora arrives earlyer than her friends.
Sora arrives earliest than her friends.

cz.st: Sora arrives ___ than her friends.

items.rule: early는 y를 i로 바꿔 earlier/earliest가 돼요. 부사 early도 같은 방식이에요.

items.good: He works harder than anyone else in the office.
items.ko: 그는 사무실의 다른 누구보다 열심히 일해요.
bad: He works more hard than anyone else in the office.
He works hardlier than anyone else in the office.
He works hardest than anyone else in the office.

cz.st: He works ___ than anyone else in the office.

items.rule: hard는 형용사와 부사의 형태가 같고 비교급은 harder예요. hardly는 '거의 ~않다'라는 다른 뜻이에요.

items.good: Of all the students, Dara studies the most carefully.
items.ko: 모든 학생 중에서 다라가 가장 꼼꼼하게 공부해요.
bad: Of all the students, Dara studies the more carefully.
Of all the students, Dara studies most careful.
Of all the students, Dara studies the carefullest.

cz.st: Of all the students, Dara studies the ___ carefully.

items.rule: 부사의 최상급은 the most + 부사예요 (carefully → the most carefully).

items.good: Which is taller, the tower or the tree?
items.ko: 탑과 나무 중 어느 것이 더 키가 커요?
bad: Which is tallest, the tower or the tree?
Which is more tall, the tower or the tree?
Which is the tall, the tower or the tree?

cz.st: Which is ___, the tower or the tree?

items.rule: 둘 중 어느 쪽이 더 ~한지 물을 때는 비교급을 써요.

items.good: Jina is the second tallest girl in our class.
items.ko: 지나는 우리 반에서 두 번째로 키가 큰 여학생이에요.
bad: Jina is the second taller girl in our class.
Jina is the tallest second girl in our class.
Jina is second tallest girl in our class.

cz.st: Jina is the second ___ girl in our class.

items.rule: 'the second + 최상급'은 '두 번째로 가장 ~한'이에요. 최상급 앞에 the를 써요.

items.good: This is the best pizza I have ever eaten.
items.ko: 이것은 내가 먹어 본 피자 중 최고예요.
bad: This is the goodest pizza I have ever eaten.
This is the better pizza I have ever eaten.
This is the most good pizza I have ever eaten.

cz.st: This is the ___ pizza I have ever eaten.

items.rule: good의 최상급은 best예요. 'ever eaten'은 지금까지 먹어 본 것 중이라는 뜻이에요.

items.good: The library is farther from my house than the park.
items.ko: 도서관은 공원보다 우리 집에서 더 멀어요.
bad: The library is far from my house than the park.
The library is more far from my house than the park.
The library is farest from my house than the park.

cz.st: The library is ___ from my house than the park.

items.rule: far의 비교급은 farther예요 (far - farther - farthest).

items.good: I have as many friends as you.
items.ko: 나는 너만큼 친구가 많아요.
bad: I have as much friends as you.
I have as many friends than you.
I have so many friends as you.

cz.st: I have as ___ friends as you.

items.rule: 셀 수 있는 명사의 수가 같을 때는 'as many + 복수 명사 + as'를 써요.

items.good: Is this bag cheaper than that one?
items.ko: 이 가방이 저것보다 더 싸요?
bad: Is this bag more cheaper than that one?
Is this bag cheapest than that one?
Is this bag cheap than that one?

cz.st: Is this bag ___ than that one?

items.rule: 의문문에서도 than 앞에는 비교급이 와요.

items.good: Soccer is by far the most popular sport at our school.
items.ko: 축구는 우리 학교에서 단연 가장 인기 있는 운동이에요.
bad: Soccer is by far most popular sport at our school.
Soccer is by far the more popular sport at our school.
Soccer is by far the popularest sport at our school.

cz.st: Soccer is by far the ___ popular sport at our school.

items.rule: by far는 최상급을 강조하여 '단연'이라는 뜻이에요. 최상급 앞에는 the를 써요.

items.good: Nothing is more important than health.
items.ko: 건강보다 더 중요한 것은 없어요.
bad: Nothing is most important than health.
Nothing is more important that health.
Nothing is importanter than health.

cz.st: Nothing is ___ important than health.

items.rule: 'Nothing is more ~ than …'은 '…보다 더 ~한 것은 없다'로, 비교급으로 최상급의 뜻을 나타내요.

items.good: Of the three cakes, the chocolate cake is the sweetest.
items.ko: 세 케이크 중 초콜릿 케이크가 가장 달아요.
bad: Of the three cakes, the chocolate cake is the sweeter.
Of the three cakes, the chocolate cake is sweetest.
Of the three cakes, the chocolate cake is the sweetest than.

cz.st: Of the three cakes, the chocolate cake is the ___.

items.rule: 셋 이상 중에서는 최상급을 써요. 최상급 앞에 the가 필요해요.

items.good: This phone is less expensive than that one.
items.ko: 이 휴대폰은 저것보다 덜 비싸요.
bad: This phone is less expensive as that one.
This phone is least expensive than that one.
This phone is lesser expensive than that one.

cz.st: This phone is ___ expensive than that one.

items.rule: 'less + 원급 + than'은 '~보다 덜 …한'이에요. least는 최상급에 써요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
A turtle is ___ than a rabbit.
items.why: than이 있으니 비교급 slower가 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Of all the animals at the zoo, the giraffe is the ___.
items.why: 동물원의 모든 동물 중에서는 the + 최상급이에요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
This bag is ___ than that one, so I will buy it.
items.why: than이 있으므로 비교급 cheaper가 알맞고, more를 중복하지 않아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Mina is the ___ girl in our class. She is always smiling.
items.why: y를 i로 바꾸고 -est를 붙인 happiest가 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
My grandmother cooks ___ than my mother.
items.why: '~보다 더 잘'은 well의 비교급 better를 써요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Seoul has ___ people than my hometown.
items.why: many/much의 비교급은 more예요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Your cold is bad, but mine is even ___.
items.why: bad의 비교급은 worse예요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
It was the ___ day of my life!
items.why: good의 최상급은 best예요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Math is ___ difficult than science for me.
items.why: difficult는 긴 형용사라서 more difficult than으로 비교해요.

items.q: 다음 중 beautiful의 비교급과 최상급을 바르게 짝지은 것은?
items.why: 긴 형용사는 more/most를 앞에 붙여요.

items.q: 다음 중 big의 변화가 바른 것은?
items.why: 단모음 + 단자음이므로 자음을 겹쳐 쓰고 -er/-est를 붙여요.

items.q: 다음 중 happy의 변화가 바른 것은?
items.why: y를 i로 바꾸고 -er, -est를 붙여요.

items.q: 다음 중 비교급·최상급 짝이 잘못된 것은?
items.why: far는 farther - farthest(또는 further - furthest)로 변해요.

items.q: 다음 형용사 중 비교급을 만들 때 more를 쓰는 것은?
items.why: careful은 2음절 이상의 -ful 형용사라 more careful이 돼요.

items.q: Tom is taller than Ben. 와 뜻이 같은 문장은?
o: Ben is as tall as Tom.
items.why: Tom이 더 크면 Ben은 더 작아요.

items.q: Anna is older than Joe. Joe is older than Kim. Who is the youngest?
items.why: 나이 순서는 Anna > Joe > Kim이므로 Kim이 가장 어려요.

items.q: My bag is lighter than yours. 의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
items.why: lighter than은 '~보다 더 가벼운'이에요.

items.q: This pen is not as expensive as that one. 과 뜻이 같은 문장은?
o: That pen is more expensive than this one.
This pen is more expensive than that one.
This pen is the most expensive.
items.why: 이 펜이 저 펜만큼 비싸지 않다는 것은 저 펜이 더 비싸다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Lisa runs faster than Mia. Mia runs faster than Eve. 다음 중 맞는 설명은?
o: Mia is the fastest of the three.
Eve is the slowest of the three.
items.why: 속도 순서는 Lisa > Mia > Eve예요.

items.q: Book A costs $5, Book B costs $8, and Book C costs $6. 다음 중 맞는 설명은?
o: Book A is more expensive than Book C.
Book B is the most expensive.
Book B is cheaper than Book A.
items.why: 가격은 B($8) > C($6) > A($5)이므로 B가 가장 비싸요.

items.q: The soup is as hot as the tea. 의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
items.why: as ~ as는 '~만큼 ...한'이에요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
'이 방은 저 방보다 더 커요.'
o: This room is the biggest than that room.
This room is more big that room.
This room bigger than that room.
This room is bigger than that room.
items.why: 비교급 bigger와 than을 쓰고 be동사를 빠뜨리지 않아요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
'그는 우리 반에서 가장 키가 큰 학생이에요.'
o: He is the tallest student in our class.
He is a taller student in our class.
He is the most tall student in our class.
He is the tallest student than our class.
items.why: 최상급은 'the + -est + 명사 + in + 집단'이에요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
'날씨가 점점 추워지고 있어요.'
o: It is getting cold and cold.
It is getting colder and colder.
It is getting colder than colder.
items.why: '비교급 and 비교급'이 '점점 더'를 나타내요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
'더 연습할수록 더 잘하게 돼요.'
o: More you practice, better you get.
The most you practice, the best you get.
The more you practice, the better you get.
The more you practice, the best you get.
items.why: 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급' 구문이에요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
'나는 오빠만큼 빨리 달릴 수 있어요.'
o: I can run as fast as my brother.
I can run as faster as my brother.
I can run as fast than my brother.
I can run so fast my brother.
items.why: 같은 정도는 'as + 원급 + as'로 나타내요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
'이 가방이 셋 중에서 가장 비싸요.'
o: This bag is more expensive of the three.
This bag is the expensivest of the three.
This bag is most expensive in the three.
This bag is the most expensive of the three.
items.why: 셋 중에서는 the most expensive of the three를 써요.

items.q: She is the most tall girl in our class. 를 바르게 고친 문장은?
o: She is the taller girl in our class.
She is the tallest girl in our class.
She is most tall girl in our class.
She is the tallest girl than our class.
items.why: 짧은 형용사는 most 대신 -est를 붙여요.

items.q: Today is more hotter than yesterday. 를 바르게 고친 문장은?
o: Today is most hotter than yesterday.
items.why: 비교급 표시를 두 번 하지 않고 hotter 하나만 써요.

items.q: He runs more fast than I do. 를 바르게 고친 문장은?
o: He runs fastest than I do.
He runs more faster than I do.
He runs the faster than I do.
He runs faster than I do.
items.why: fast는 짧은 단어라 faster로 비교급을 만들어요.

items.q: I am gooder at math than my friend. 를 바르게 고친 문장은?
o: I am better at math than my friend.
I am best at math than my friend.
I am more good at math than my friend.
I am gooder at math then my friend.
items.why: good의 비교급은 better예요.

items.q: This is the baddest cold I have ever had. 를 바르게 고친 문장은?
o: This is the worse cold I have ever had.
This is the most bad cold I have ever had.
This is the worst cold I have ever had.
This is the badest cold I have ever had.
items.why: bad의 최상급은 worst예요.

items.q: Our new teacher is as kind than the old one. 를 바르게 고친 문장은?
o: Our new teacher is kinder as the old one.
Our new teacher is as kinder than the old one.
Our new teacher is as kind as the old one.
Our new teacher is so kind than the old one.
items.why: 'as + 원급 + as' 구문이에요.

items.q: The harder you study, the more good your grades will be. 를 바르게 고친 문장은?
o: The harder you study, the better your grades will be.
The harder you study, the best your grades will be.
The hardest you study, the better your grades will be.
Harder you study, better your grades will be.
items.why: good의 비교급은 better이고 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급'을 써요.

items.q: It is very colder today than yesterday. 를 바르게 고친 문장은?
o: It is very cold today than yesterday.
It is more colder today than yesterday.
It is coldest today than yesterday.
It is much colder today than yesterday.
items.why: 비교급은 much로 강조하고 very로는 강조하지 않아요.

items.q:
다음 중 비교급 앞에 쓸 수 없는 말은?
This box is ___ bigger than that one.
items.why: much, a lot, even, far는 비교급을 강조하지만 very는 쓸 수 없어요.

items.q:
다음 빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
He is the smartest student ___.
items.why: 최상급 뒤에 범위를 나타내는 in the school이 와요.

items.q: Which sentence tells us that Tom and Ben are the same height?
o: Tom is not as tall as Ben.
Tom is as tall as Ben.
items.why: 'as + 원급 + as'는 같은 정도를 나타내요.

items.q: 다음 중 철자가 바른 비교급은? (thin)
items.why: 단모음 + 단자음이므로 n을 겹쳐 thinner가 돼요.

items.q: 다음 중 철자가 바른 비교급은? (noisy)
items.why: y를 i로 바꾸고 -er을 붙여요.

items.q: 다음 중 철자가 바른 최상급은? (heavy)
items.why: y를 i로 바꾸고 -est를 붙여요.

items.q: 다음 중 철자가 바른 최상급은? (sad)
items.why: 단모음 + 단자음이므로 d를 겹쳐 saddest가 돼요.

items.q: 다음 중 more를 붙여 비교급을 만드는 부사는?
items.why: -ly로 끝나는 부사는 more carefully처럼 more를 붙여요.

items.q:
Sam is 150 cm, Ann is 160 cm, and Joy is 155 cm. 빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Ann is the ___ of the three.
items.why: 세 명 중 가장 큰 사람은 Ann이에요.

items.q:
Tom sleeps 7 hours and Jin sleeps 9 hours. 빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Jin sleeps ___ hours than Tom.
items.why: hours 앞의 비교급은 more예요.

items.q: Monday was 20 degrees, Tuesday was 25 degrees, and Wednesday was 18 degrees. Which day was the coldest?
items.why: 18도인 수요일이 가장 추웠어요.

items.q: A is bigger than B. 과 뜻이 다른 문장은?
o: B is not as big as A.
items.why: A가 더 크면 B가 더 크다는 문장만 의미가 달라요.

items.q: Better late than never. 의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
items.why: never(전혀 안 함)보다 late(늦게 함)가 더 낫다는 속담이에요.

items.q: The sooner, the better. 의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
items.why: 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급'은 '~할수록 더 ...하다'예요.

items.q: Two heads are better than one. 의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
o: 두 사람이 함께 생각하면 더 좋아요.
items.why: 두 사람의 지혜가 한 사람보다 낫다는 속담이에요.

items.q: Actions speak louder than words. 의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
o: 행동이 말보다 더 큰 힘이 있어요.
items.why: speak louder than words는 말보다 행동이 더 중요하다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 'bigger'와 반대되는 뜻의 비교급은?
items.why: bigger의 반대는 smaller예요.

items.q: This watch is ___ expensive ___ that one. 빈칸에 차례로 알맞은 말은?
items.why: 'more + 원급 + than'이 비교급 구문이에요.

items.q: 빈칸에 the가 필요한 문장은?
o: Jun is ___ as young as Min.
Jun is ___ youngest in the team.
items.why: 최상급 앞에는 the가 필요하지만 비교급과 as ~ as에는 필요하지 않아요.

items.q: Sam is ___ tall ___ his father now. (아버지와 키가 같아요) 빈칸에 차례로 알맞은 말은?
items.why: 같은 정도는 as ~ as예요.

items.q:
Tom's score is 90 and Jina's score is 90. 빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Tom's score is ___ Jina's.
items.why: 점수가 같으므로 the same as가 알맞아요.

items.title: Two Ways to School
items.text: Mina has two ways to get to school. The bus is faster than walking, but it is more crowded in the morning. Walking takes twenty-five minutes, while the bus takes only ten. However, the bus costs money, and walking is free. On sunny days, Mina prefers to walk because the streets near the river are quieter and the air is fresher. On rainy days she takes the bus, since it is the driest and safest choice. Her friend Hojun lives farther away, so he always rides his bike. He says it is the best way to wake up before class.

qs.q: How long does the bus ride take?
qs.why: 버스는 단 10분이 걸린다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does Mina walk on sunny days?
o: Walking is faster than taking the crowded bus then.
The bus costs too much money on sunny days.
She likes to meet Hojun along the way.
The river streets are quiet and the air is fresh.
qs.why: 맑은 날에는 강가 길이 더 조용하고 공기가 상쾌해서 걸어요.

qs.q: The word "crowded" is closest in meaning to ___.
qs.why: crowded는 사람이 많아 붐비는 상태를 뜻해요.

qs.q: Which is true about Hojun?
o: He takes the bus to school on rainy days.
He walks to school with Mina.
He lives farther from school than Mina.
He thinks the bus is the best way.
qs.why: Hojun은 더 멀리 살아서 항상 자전거를 타요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to ride a bike safely when it is raining
Why walking is better than any other exercise
The different ways Mina and her friend travel to school
A new bus line that opens near the river
qs.why: 버스, 도보, 자전거를 비교하며 등교 방법을 설명하는 글이에요.

items.title: A Letter to Grandpa
items.text: Hi Grandpa, I miss you! Our new apartment is smaller than our old house, but I like it more. My room is the smallest in the apartment, yet it has the biggest window, so I can see the park every morning. School is also different. My new school is bigger, and the classes are more interesting. The food is not as good as Grandma's cooking, of course! Dad says the subway here is cleaner and faster than the buses in our old town. Please visit us soon. The park is prettiest in October, when all the leaves turn red. Love, Sora

qs.q: Why did Sora write this email?
o: To tell her grandfather about her new home and school
To ask her grandfather for his cooking advice
To invite her grandfather to a school event soon
To complain about the subway in her town
qs.why: 새 집과 학교 이야기를 전하며 방문을 청하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What is special about Sora's room?
o: It is bigger than her old room.
It is the quietest in the apartment.
It is next to the subway station.
qs.why: 가장 작지만 가장 큰 창문이 있어 공원이 보여요.

qs.q: Which sentence is true about Sora's new school?
o: Its food is better than Grandma's cooking.
It is bigger than her old school.
Its classes are less interesting than before.
It is closer to Grandpa's house now.
qs.why: 새 학교는 더 크다(bigger)고 했어요.

qs.q: How does Sora seem to feel about her new life?
qs.why: 집과 학교의 좋은 점을 이야기하는 것으로 보아 만족하고 있어요.

qs.q: When is the park prettiest?
qs.why: 10월에 잎이 모두 붉게 물든다고 했어요.

items.title: Cats or Dogs?
items.text: Many families ask which pet is easier to care for, a cat or a dog. Dogs usually need more time than cats. They must go for walks every day, even when it is cold or rainy. Cats, on the other hand, can stay at home alone for longer, and they clean themselves. However, dogs are often friendlier and more active, so they can be better partners for sports. Cats are quieter, which is good for apartments with thin walls. In the end, the best pet depends on your family's schedule. A busy family may choose a cat, but a family that loves outdoor activities may be happier with a dog.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: The best pet depends on how a family lives.
Dogs are always better pets than cats.
Cats are the cleanest animals in the world.
Walking every day is bad for dogs.
qs.why: 고양이와 개를 비교한 뒤 가족의 생활에 따라 달라진다고 결론 내려요.

qs.q: Why might a cat suit an apartment with thin walls?
o: It is more active than a dog.
It is quieter than a dog.
It is smaller than most dogs.
qs.why: 고양이는 더 조용해서 벽이 얇은 아파트에 좋다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which family would probably be happiest with a dog?
o: One that is away from home all day long
One that dislikes any noise or barking at home
One that enjoys hiking and running together
One that lives far from every park
qs.why: 야외 활동을 좋아하는 가족에게 개가 더 어울린다고 했어요.

qs.q: In this passage, "on the other hand" is used to ___.
qs.why: on the other hand는 앞과 다른 면을 소개할 때 써요.

qs.q: Which is true about cats according to the passage?
o: They need to go out for walks in the rain.
They are usually friendlier than most dogs.
They are more active than dogs.
They can stay home alone longer than dogs.
qs.why: 고양이는 더 오래 혼자 집에 있을 수 있다고 했어요.

items.title: Sports Day
items.text: Friday, May 12. Today was Sports Day, and it was the most exciting day of the term. The morning was hotter than I expected, so everyone drank a lot of water. In the relay race, our team started badly because the first runner dropped the baton. Jiho, our last runner, was the fastest boy in the grade, and he ran harder than ever. We did not win, but we finished second, which was much better than last year. I was not as sad as I thought I would be. Our teacher said that trying together is more important than winning.

qs.q: What went wrong at the start of the relay?
o: Jiho fell down near the finish line.
The first runner dropped the baton.
The team ran in the wrong lane at first.
qs.why: 첫 주자가 바통을 떨어뜨렸다고 했어요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel at the end of the day?
qs.why: 2등이었지만 생각만큼 슬프지 않고 만족스러워해요.

qs.q: Where did the writer's team finish?
qs.why: 2등으로 들어왔다고 했어요.

qs.q: "He ran harder than ever" means Jiho ___.
o: tried with more effort than before
ran on a harder track than before
found the race more difficult than before
qs.why: harder than ever는 그 어느 때보다 열심히 했다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the teacher's idea show?
o: Winning is the only real goal of Sports Day.
Relay races are easier than other events.
Working together matters more than the result.
qs.why: 함께 노력하는 것이 이기는 것보다 중요하다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Choose a Club
items.text: This term we have three after-school clubs. The Art Club meets on Mondays and is the cheapest, at only 5,000 won a month. The Robot Club meets on Wednesdays, and it costs more than the Art Club because students use special kits. The Soccer Club is the most popular club, so it has the largest number of members. It meets on Fridays and the fee is 8,000 won. Students who join two clubs get a lower price for the second one. If you are not sure, you can visit each club once for free. Sign up with Ms. Han before September 5.

qs.q: Which club is the cheapest?
qs.why: 미술 클럽이 가장 싸다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does the Robot Club cost more than the Art Club?
qs.why: 특별한 키트를 사용하기 때문에 더 비싸요.

qs.q: Who should students sign up with?
qs.why: 신청은 Ms. Han에게 한다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can a student do if they are not sure which club to join?
o: Join two clubs at a lower price for one
Visit each club once without paying
Wait until the next term starts
Ask the Soccer Club to decide
qs.why: 확신이 없으면 각 클럽을 한 번 무료로 방문할 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does "fee" mean in this notice?
qs.why: fee는 어떤 일에 내는 돈을 뜻해요.

items.title: Lightning and Thunder
items.text: During a storm, you see lightning before you hear thunder. Why? Light travels much faster than sound. Light moves hundreds of thousands of times faster than sound in the air, so it reaches your eyes almost at once. Sound is slower, so it reaches your ears a few seconds later. The farther away the storm is, the longer the gap between the flash and the noise. Some students count the seconds between them to guess the distance. However, if the flash and the thunder come together, the storm is very close and it is safest to go inside quickly.

qs.q: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
o: Thunder happens after the storm ends.
Our eyes work harder than our ears.
qs.why: 빛이 소리보다 훨씬 빠르게 이동하기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What do some students do to guess how far a storm is?
o: Count the seconds between the flash and the thunder
Measure the size of the lightning with a ruler
Listen for the loudest sound in the sky
Watch how fast the dark clouds are moving
qs.why: 번개와 천둥 사이의 초를 센다고 했어요.

qs.q: If the flash and the thunder come at the same time, what is probably true?
o: The sound is faster than light.
qs.why: 동시에 오면 폭풍이 매우 가깝다고 했어요.

qs.q: The word "gap" in the passage means ___.
qs.why: gap은 두 사건 사이의 간격을 뜻해요.

items.title: Pip the Robot
items.text: Mina built a small robot called Pip for the science fair. At first, Pip was slower than the other robots, and it kept turning left. Mina felt worried because her friend Dan's robot was the fastest in the class. She stayed after school for three days and changed Pip's wheels. Little by little, Pip became faster and more stable. On the day of the fair, Dan's robot won first prize, but Pip got the prize for the most creative design. Mina was surprised and happy. She told Dan, "Your robot is faster than mine, but I learned more from building mine." Dan smiled and agreed.

qs.q: What did Mina do to improve Pip?
o: She changed its wheels after school.
She bought a faster battery online.
She asked Dan to rebuild the robot.
She painted it a brighter color.
qs.why: 방과 후에 사흘 동안 바퀴를 바꿨어요.

qs.q: Why was Mina worried at first?
o: She did not have enough time to finish
Dan told her not to join the fair
Her teacher did not like robots.
Pip was slow and kept turning left.
qs.why: Pip이 느리고 계속 왼쪽으로 돌았기 때문이에요.

qs.q: Which prize did Pip win?
o: The prize for the fastest robot of all
The prize for the most creative design
The prize for the best teamwork in class
The prize for the safest wheels
qs.why: Pip은 가장 창의적인 디자인 상을 받았어요.

qs.q: What does Mina's last speech suggest?
o: She wants a faster robot than Dan's.
She values learning more than winning.
She thinks Dan did not deserve first prize.
She is disappointed in her robot.
qs.why: Dan의 로봇이 더 빠르지만 자신은 더 많이 배웠다고 말해요.

qs.q: The word "stable" in the passage is closest in meaning to ___.
qs.why: stable은 흔들리지 않고 안정적이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Two Beaches
items.text: Last summer our family visited two beaches. Sunny Bay was larger and more crowded, with many shops and restaurants. The sand was softer there, but the water was colder than I expected. Pine Cove, on the other hand, was smaller and much quieter. We saw fewer people, and the sea was warmer and clearer, so we could see small fish near our feet. My brother liked Sunny Bay best because there was more to do. I preferred Pine Cove, since it was the most relaxing place of our trip. Next year, we plan to spend two days at each beach and compare them again.

qs.q: Which beach had warmer water?
qs.why: Pine Cove의 바다가 더 따뜻하고 맑았다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why did the writer's brother like Sunny Bay best?
o: It was quieter than Pine Cove.
There were more things to do.
qs.why: 할 것이 더 많았기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What kind of traveler is the writer?
qs.why: 조용하고 편안한 Pine Cove를 선호했어요.

qs.q: The word "relaxing" is closest in meaning to ___.
qs.why: relaxing은 마음이 편안해지는 느낌을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does the family plan to do next year?
o: Visit only Sunny Bay for the whole week
Move to a small town near Pine Cove
Stay at both beaches and compare them again
qs.why: 각 해변에서 이틀씩 머물며 다시 비교할 계획이에요.

items.title: Favorite Lunch Survey
items.text: Our class asked 30 students about their favorite school lunch. Pizza was the most popular choice, with 12 votes. Bibimbap came second with 9 votes, which was three fewer than pizza. Fried chicken received 6 votes, and only 3 students chose noodle soup. Many students said that pizza is tastier than the other foods, but some said bibimbap is healthier. The teacher added that the school will serve the top two foods more often next month. Students who like noodle soup were disappointed, but the teacher promised to try a new recipe that may be more popular.

qs.q: How many students chose bibimbap?
qs.why: 비빔밥은 9표로 2등이었어요.

qs.q: Which statement matches the survey?
o: Bibimbap got more votes than pizza did.
Fried chicken got twice as many votes as noodle soup.
Noodle soup came in second place overall.
Pizza got fewer votes than fried chicken.
qs.why: 닭튀김 6표는 국수 3표의 두 배예요.

qs.q: Why do some students prefer bibimbap?
o: They think it is tastier than pizza.
It is cheaper than other foods.
qs.why: 일부 학생은 비빔밥이 더 건강에 좋다고 말했어요.

qs.q: What will the school do next month?
o: Serve pizza and bibimbap more often
Stop serving noodle soup for good
Ask students to vote one more time
Make fried chicken the main lunch
qs.why: 상위 두 음식을 더 자주 제공할 거예요.

qs.q: Why will the teacher try a new recipe?
o: To make pizza healthier for students
To save money on school lunches
To make noodle soup more popular
qs.why: 국수를 좋아하는 학생들이 실망해서 더 인기 있는 새 조리법을 시도해요.

items.title: Sleep Matters
items.text: Teenagers need more sleep than adults, usually about nine hours a night. However, many students sleep less because of homework, phones, and early classes. Doctors say that sleeping late makes it harder to focus the next day. A student who sleeps eight hours often remembers more than one who sleeps only five. To sleep better, try to keep a regular bedtime, turn off screens an hour earlier, and avoid heavy food at night. The earlier you go to bed, the easier it is to wake up. It may feel difficult at first, but after a week most people feel more energetic and in a better mood.

qs.q: About how much sleep do teenagers usually need?
qs.why: 십대는 보통 하룻밤에 약 9시간이 필요하다고 했어요.

qs.q: What do doctors say about sleeping late?
o: It makes it harder to focus the next day.
It helps students remember more at school.
It makes people wake up very early.
It improves your mood in the morning.
qs.why: 늦게 자면 다음 날 집중하기 더 어렵다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which student will probably remember the most?
o: One who sleeps only five hours
qs.why: 8시간 자는 학생이 5시간 자는 학생보다 더 많이 기억한다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which advice is given in the passage?
o: Eat a big dinner right before bed.
Turn off screens an hour earlier.
Sleep late on school days to rest.
Go to bed later each night.
qs.why: 화면을 한 시간 일찍 끄라고 조언해요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to finish your homework much faster
Why sleep matters and how to get more of it
Why doctors dislike early school classes
Which foods give people the most energy
qs.why: 수면의 중요성과 잘 자는 방법을 설명하는 글이에요.

items.exko: 내 휴대폰과 네 휴대폰은 매우 비슷해요.
